  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.5,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R36"],
      "pins": ["R36.1", "R36.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R36 is valued \"24k\" (SPICE: `R36 VOUTN VOUTP 24k`), but its selected part is an FRC0805J240TSD (LCSC C2930261) described as a 24Ω resistor, with footprint R_0805 and a 125mW rating.",
      "expected": "A value of 24k should be paired with a 24kΩ part. If the part is 24Ω, the value should read 24R. The part, value and description should agree with each other.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R36\") (value \"24k\") (footprint \"Resistor_SMD:R_0805_2012Metric\") ... (description \" 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"MPN\") \"FRC0805J240TSD\")"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R36 VOUTN VOUTP 24k"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the 24Ω part is fitted, it places a very low resistance across the VOUTP/VOUTN supercap-style output. This would draw a large current and overheat the 125mW part. If 24k was intended, the wrong part was sourced and the bleed or sense path will not behave as designed.",
      "confidence": 0.5
    },
    {
      "category": "bridged_nets",
      "components": ["D30", "R60"],
      "pins": ["D30.4", "D30.2", "R60.2"],
      "nets": ["ESTOP_OUT", "LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV"],
      "observed": "Both ends of the second LED channel of dual LED D30 end up on ESTOP_OUT. Pin 4 (A2, anode) is on ESTOP_OUT. Pin 2 (K2, cathode) goes through R60 to ESTOP_OUT. The first channel is wired correctly: A1 on LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV, K1 through R59 to GND. The LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV net does not include D30 pin 4.",
      "expected": "The anode of the second channel should be on the LED supply net LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV, like the anodes of D8, D28 and D29, with the cathode driven through R60 to ESTOP_OUT.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"67\") (name \"ESTOP_OUT\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"A2\") (pintype \"input\")) ... (node (ref \"R60\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"U36\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"Y\") (pintype \"output\")))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"31\") (name \"/LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV\") ... (node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"3\") (pinfunction \"A1\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R60 Net-_D30-K2_ ESTOP_OUT 130"}
      ],
      "impact": "The second LED in D30 is shorted out by its own series resistor, so its status indicator never lights. The e-stop output node is also loaded by an unintended LED path.",
      "confidence": 0.4
    },
    {
      "category": "polarity",
      "components": ["D12", "R13", "U18"],
      "pins": ["D12.1", "D12.2", "R13.2", "U18.4"],
      "nets": ["Net-(D12-K)", "Net-(D12-A)", "+3V3", "Net-(U18-Y)"],
      "observed": "D12 (green LED) has its cathode (pin 1) on the R13 side, which is tied to +3V3, and its anode (pin 2) on the open-drain output U18 Y. This is reversed relative to the otherwise identical indicator D17, which has its anode on the +3V3 side and its cathode on U19 Y. Current would flow from the 3.3V side into the cathode, so the LED cannot conduct when U18 pulls Y low. R13 is 27Ω, which would also drive about 40 mA if the LED were oriented correctly.",
      "expected": "The TX indicator D12 should be oriented like D17, with anode toward +3V3 through a current-limit resistor and cathode on the open-drain output, so it lights when Y is pulled low.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"112\") (name \"Net-(D12-K)\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"D12\") (pin \"1\") (pinfunction \"K\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"R13\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\")))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"111\") (name \"Net-(D12-A)\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"D12\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"U18\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"Y\") (pintype \"output\")))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"116\") (name \"Net-(D17-K)\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"D17\") (pin \"1\") (pinfunction \"K\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"U19\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"Y\") (pintype \"output\")))"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "`board_TODO.txt`: \"invert CAN TX/RX LED polarity either by using inverting buffer part number or by rewiring input\""}
      ],
      "impact": "The CAN transmit activity indicator never lights, so a visible diagnostic is lost. The spec lists CAN LED polarity as an open question, so this may be the known issue rather than a new fault. The asymmetry with D17 is the reason it is still flagged.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The netlist shows a 24Ω-part with a 24k value on R36, a second LED channel in D30 whose anode is tied to ESTOP_OUT with its own resistor across the same net, and a TX indicator D12 that is reverse-oriented relative to its mirror D17. The first is a clear value/part mismatch and the second is a wiring error, so these are the most likely deviations from the intended design."
}
